haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors never reach the document service or Postgres. They go through Redis keys and the presence pub/sub channel.
haiku-low.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms per connection. The node silently drops any cursor that arrives sooner.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor and draws nothing until its appliedRev reaches that rev, then draws it.
haiku-low.q4: It calls transformPosition to move the position forward. If that throws HistoryGone, the cursor is dropped and the browser waits for the next one.
haiku-low.q5: One list entry and one caret, keyed by userId, using the most recent cursor from any connection. They disappear when their last connection leaves or expires.
haiku-low.q6: Clean tab close: others see the leave within 2 s. Gateway node death: the user disappears about 35 s after the crash, within the 45 s requirement.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis: a hash doc:{docId}:conns with one field per connId, plus conn and cursor keys per connection. Pongs and accepted cursors refresh the keys to a 30 s TTL.
haiku-low.q8: Surviving nodes' sweepers, every 5 s, remove rows whose conn key expired. The sweeper publishes a leave on presence:{docId}, which reaches other clients via the nodes.
haiku-low.q9: The sender's node stores the cursor and publishes it on presence:{docId}. Every subscribed node, including the sender's own, forwards it to its local browsers.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes to presence:{docId} before reading the snapshot, so nothing sent during loading is missed. Duplicate joins are harmless because the list is keyed by userId.
haiku-low.q11: The snapshot includes each connection's last cursor stored in Redis, so an idle user's caret appears immediately on join.
haiku-low.q12: The browser keeps the highest accepted seq per connection and discards equal or lower seq cursors, including held ones. A newer accepted cursor drops older held ones.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never reach the document service or Postgres; they go via Redis (stored key plus pub/sub).
sonnet.q2: Server-side limit per connection: if a connection sent a cursor less than 50 ms earlier, the node silently drops the new one. (50 ms is a plan value to be tuned.)
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor and draws nothing until its appliedRev reaches rev, then draws it. Held cursors are rechecked whenever appliedRev advances.
sonnet.q4: The browser calls transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev) to move it forward. If that throws HistoryGone (history no longer kept, e.g. very old), the cursor is dropped and it waits for the next one.
sonnet.q5: One list entry and one caret per user (store keyed by userId); the caret uses the cursor from the connection whose cursor arrived most recently (seq applied per connection). They disappear only when their last connection leaves; a leave is published only if no other connections remain.
sonnet.q6: Clean close: within 2 s. Node death: worst case 35 s after the crash, inside the 45 s requirement.
sonnet.q7: In Redis: a hash doc:{docId}:conns with one field per connId (row with userId and node), plus per-connection strings conn:{connId} and cursor:{docId}:{connId} with 30 s TTL. Kept fresh by refreshing the TTL on each pong (every 10 s), and the cursor key also on each accepted cursor. The index hash rows are not renewed.
sonnet.q8: Its keys stop being refreshed and expire after 30 s. Every surviving node sweeps every 5 s, finds index rows whose conn key expired, removes the row and cursor keys via a script, and if it was the user's last connection publishes a leave on presence:{docId}. Nodes forward that leave to their browsers (sweeps are idempotent so only one leave is published).
sonnet.q9: The node stores the cursor in Redis with TTL and publishes it on presence:{docId}. Every subscribed node, including the sender's own node via its own subscription, receives it and forwards it to its own browsers. (Whether the sender's node skips echoing to the sender is NOT STATED.)
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to presence:{docId} first, before adding the user and reading the snapshot from Redis, so messages during the snapshot read are not missed. Duplicates are harmless because the list is keyed by userId.
sonnet.q11: Each connection's last cursor is stored in Redis (cursor:{docId}:{connId}, with TTL refreshed on pongs), and the snapshot on open includes it, so idle users' carets appear at once.
sonnet.q12: Each cursor carries a per-connection seq. The browser remembers the highest seq accepted per connection and discards any cursor with an equal or lower seq, including held ones; accepting a newer one drops older held cursors from that connection.
